title: Nuclear dimension and Jiang–Su stability without elementary subquotients
main_claim: Every separable nuclear A_0 satisfies dim_nuc(A_0⊗Z) ≤ 1. For a separable nuclear algebra with no nonzero elementary ideal subquotients, three conditions are equivalent: finite nuclear dimension, Z-stability, and dim_nuc ≤ 1. A further result: for every unital D with no characters, some finite maximal tensor power D^{⊗max n} contains two full orthogonal positive elements, which answers Kirchberg–Rørdam's Question 6.2.

issues.description: Two steps rest on cited results that were not checked here. The 'no characters in F(A)' step needs every matrix summand in the decomposition of 1_{F(A)} to have size at least two. The paper takes this from Winter–Zacharias Proposition 4.3 and also asserts it for nonunital A via the annihilator quotient F(A), but the cited source may only state the unital or covering-number version. If so, the nonunital form is an unproved extension, not a proved step. The same caveat applies to Robert–Tikuisis Theorem 1.2 for nonunital A.
issues.evidence: 'This is the matrix-threshold-two consequence of the covering-number bound cov(F(A))≤(d+1)^2 [WZNuclear, Definition 4.1 and Proposition 4.3]' ... 'Both assertions apply to nonunital A, with the annihilator quotient just defined.'

issues.location: sections/02_preliminaries.tex, Lemma prelim:unitary (cited as BBSTWW Lemma 5.3)
issues.description: The unitary-equivalence criterion is stated for ultraproducts of arbitrary separable unital Z-stable D_n. Its hypotheses are only that C is full and that the condition on full hereditary subalgebras holds. The paper verifies those hypotheses carefully (Corollary comm:fullness and Proposition conjugacy:hereditary). It was not checked whether the original BBSTWW lemma has an additional assumption, such as simplicity of D_n, which would not hold here (D_n = M_2(A⊗Z^3) is non-simple).
issues.evidence: 'This is [BBSTWW, Lemma 5.3], whose proof adapts the positive-element classification method of Robert–Santiago'

coverage: I read all nine sections in full, plus the README. Checked by hand: (a) Lemma lem:gaussian: the Hamming-ball bound, the Gilbert exponent log2 − log(4/3) − (1/4)log3 ≈ 0.131 > 0, the covariance and Gershgorin bound, the density-ratio bound, q^N against a net of size exp(O(n^2)), and the norm-perturbation bound ||G||·n·η_n = 1/2. (b) The tensor theorem: the commutator witness and spectral-diameter bound, uniform angle separation by compactness, the factor-product lemma, pure-state excision, the compression estimate, and fullness of h_±. (c) Section 9: no characters from order-zero functionals on M_r, the reindexing lemma, and fullness surviving under a unital homomorphism. (d) Section 3: quasicentral slicing, the rank bound from strictly positive cuts, the corner trace bound, expected-trace and rounding estimates, and orthogonal-corner norm bounds. (e) Section 4: the I_{d,d+1} order-zero construction and its trace estimate, the copy relations, the common-part construction via the multiplicative domain, localized expectation via the unique trace of Z, the w_n trace bound via λ∘T_n and the matrix-trace lemma, both large-rank cases (including the ideal argument when the rank is infinite), the scalar inequality (s−γ/16)_+(t−1/2)_+ ≤ (st−γ/32)_+, the constant bookkeeping γ/(32K) against (1/2)(γ/16)/K, and the bounded witnesses. (f) Section 5: the supporting-map diagonalization with witness bounds independent of l, extension of ideal containment, the packing identity r_s^*π(a)r_s' = δ Σ y^*Ψ(a)y, the intertwiner computation, fullness, almost unperforation via a reindexed copy of Z, the hereditary-subalgebra condition (the norm estimate 2ε+ε^2), and the dimension-function argument for f(h_0)~f(h_1). (g) Section 6: the two-colour corner approximation, stabilization, and hereditary permanence. Not independently verified: the exact statements and hypotheses of the cited external results (BCW/HKW, Gabe Theorem 3.3, BBSTWW Lemma 5.3, ERS Proposition 6.2 and the quasitrace correspondence, WZ Proposition 4.3, RT Theorem 1.2), and the companion papers used only for the Cuntz-semigroup corollary.
